Roasted figs with honey and ice cream make the perfect ending to a delicious meal. Make roasted figs with honey and ice cream with help from an executive chef in this free video clip.

Expert: Arthur Wall
Contact: www.garconsf.com/index.php?page=about_us
Bio: Arthur Wall was named to the position of Executive Chef in Febuary 2010 by Garcon Bistro.
Filmmaker: Steven Watkins

Series Description: Working figs into your favorite meals and appetizers is a really delicious way to add additional flavors. Find out more about cooking with figs with help from an executive chef in this free video series.

summary.brief: Chef Arthur Wall sautés sliced figs in a honey‑water caramel, finishes with butter, and serves them over chilled crème‑fresh gelato garnished with basil.
summary.detailed: After a brief musical intro, Chef Arthur Wall greets the viewer and explains that he will make sautéed figs with a simple honey‑caramel sauce. He slices fresh Adriatic figs lengthwise, preheats a sauté pan, adds two tablespoons of honey and two tablespoons of water to create a light caramel, then places the fig halves in the pan and cooks them about thirty seconds on each side. He finishes the pan by stirring in roughly half a tablespoon of butter to keep the sauce smooth, removes the pan to let the figs cool slightly, and scoops a couple of servings of crème‑fresh gelato into a chilled glass. He tops the gelato with the warm honey‑butter figs and sauce, adds a fresh basil leaf as garnish, and presents the completed dessert on a white plate before the video transitions to the eHow branding and final credits.

nodes.plm_action: cut figs in half
nodes.plm_caption: In a restaurant kitchen, a chef demonstrates how to slice a fig. The segment begins with the chef's face and name superimposed onto the bottom of the screen, then fades out on his name, and then a small screen that shows an advertisement for ehow food goes on screen with white, green, and red lettering. The second shot shows the chef in the kitchen with a title graphic superimposed below him that reads, "arthur wall ehow chef." Once he's done with this shot, there is a cut to the chef holding a knife and cutting a fig on a white board. He first places the uncut fruit on the board, then removes the stem end, removes two slices from one side and cuts the outer layer of the fig off. Then, he removes the skin and cuts the first one in half. He sets the skin aside on the board, then cuts the second half of the skin, leaving a small, uncut section of the stem. He pushes the uncut stem back, turns the knife horizontally, and continues cutting the outside layer of the second half of the figure into two pieces, keeping the uncut stem in place and removing it from the board. He continues this process until he has four pieces that he pushes away from the board, and then he cuts the other half of the fruit, keeping the cut stem and removing the second uncut stem. When he is done, he sets the board on the counter and removes the skin and the second cut stem. Overall, the video is a few seconds long.

summary.brief: Chef Arthur Wall introduces himself and demonstrates how to slice fresh figs on a cutting board.
summary.detailed: The clip opens with an eHow animation that shows the word “food” on a red background and the eHow logo, then a translucent banner appears with the chef’s name, Arthur Wall, and his face is briefly overlaid before fading. The scene cuts to a kitchen where the chef, wearing a white coat and apron, stands at a white countertop that holds a block of white cheese and several whole green figs on a cutting board. He picks up a fig, cuts off the stem end, trims away two outer slices and removes the skin, then halves the fruit lengthwise. Each half is sliced horizontally into quarters while keeping the remaining stem in place, and the sliced pieces are pushed aside on the board with the removed skins and stems set aside, completing the preparation of sliced figs as soft background music plays.

action.detailed: Slice the figs by removing the stem, trimming off the outer layer, halving them lengthwise, and quartering each half while arranging the pieces on the cutting board.

     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where

   - at least one target domain matches
